title: JRE 2264 - Lenval Logan & Jason Sands
guestBio: Lenval Logan is a retired U.S. Air Force intelligence analyst and former UAP Task Force member. He is the CEO of Phenom LLC, which develops the Phenom app for reporting UAP and paranormal sightings. Logan appears in James Fox's documentary, "The Program," Dan Farah and Lue Elizondo's "The Age of Disclosure," and season five of The History Channel's "The Proof Is Out There."
tldr: Lenval Logan and Jason Sands are former U.S. Air Force intelligence officials who worked on UAP programs and discuss their experiences with classified UFO investigations
Logan developed the Phenom app to crowdsource UAP and paranormal sighting reports, creating a database of civilian encounters
Both guests detail their involvement in official government UAP task forces and the evolution of government transparency on the topic
Discussion covers the credibility crisis in UFO reporting and how to distinguish genuine sightings from misidentifications
Logan appears in multiple documentaries including James Fox's 'The Program' and 'The Age of Disclosure' discussing UAP disclosure
The conversation explores why military and intelligence communities have historically suppressed UAP information and what's changing in 2024
recap:
Joe brings on Lenval Logan and Jason Sands, two former Air Force intelligence professionals with legitimate credentials in government UAP programs. This isn't some random conspiracy theorist podcast. These are guys who actually worked in classified environments dealing with this stuff, and they're walking Joe through what they experienced and what they're doing now.

Logan's the CEO of Phenom LLC and has created an app literally designed to collect UAP sighting reports from everyday people. The idea is solid: if you're going to study this phenomenon, you need data, and a lot of valuable data comes from regular people who actually see things. Logan's been featured in serious documentaries like 'The Program' by James Fox, 'The Age of Disclosure' with Dan Farah and Lue Elizondo, and shows up on History Channel's 'The Proof Is Out There.' He's not some fringe character.

The conversation digs into why the government locked this stuff down for so long and what's actually changing now. Sands brings his own experience as a legacy UAP program member, meaning he was part of the older, deeper programs before they became public knowledge. They discuss the structural reasons why this information was compartmentalized so heavily and why disclosure is happening in phases rather than all at once.

What's interesting about the discussion is how both guys talk about the credibility problem in UFO reporting. Not everything people report is real, and they acknowledge that straight up. The trick is having actual methodology to separate signal from noise. That's where the Phenom app comes in. It's not just collection, it's designed with filters and verification layers to help identify legitimate reports.

They touch on the generational shift in how the military and intelligence community views UAPs. The older guard was skeptical or suppressive. The newer generation is more willing to engage with the data scientifically. That shift is real and it's accelerating.

The whole conversation sits in this interesting space between government accountability and legitimate national security concerns. These aren't guys pushing a narrative. They're presenting data and their professional experience, and they're doing it in a way that respects both the seriousness of the topic and the legitimate questions people have.
